successCriteria.description: The LeaveBalance entity interface is exported from the leave-balance module and exposes exactly the fields id, employeeId, policyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status ('ACTIVE'|'EXHAUSTED'|'CLOSED'), createdAt, updatedAt — with status as an inline string union (no shared-types enum import).

The ILeaveBalanceRepository interface declares findById, findByEmployeeId, findByEmployeeAndPolicy, findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear, create, update, and upsert; the concrete PgLeaveBalanceRepository class implements it and compiles under strict TypeScript with no `any` types.

findById/findByEmployeeId/findByEmployeeAndPolicy/findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear return a mapped LeaveBalance when a valid row is found, return null when no row matches, return null when the row fails the type guard, and propagate underlying database errors.
create persists a new leave_balances row (generating id and timestamps), returns the mapped LeaveBalance, and throws a typed error when the insert returns no row or a row that fails the type guard.

update builds a dynamic SET clause from the provided partial fields, appends updated_at, returns the updated LeaveBalance (or null when not found), and delegates to findById when no fields are supplied.

upsert performs an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) DO UPDATE that inserts a new balance when no conflict occurs and updates total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, status, and updated_at when a conflict occurs, returning the mapped LeaveBalance in both paths.

The Jest unit test suite at tests/unit/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.repository.test.ts covers every repository method for success, not-found, type-guard-failure, and error propagation, plus upsert insert-path and conflict-path, and the full suite passes via `npm run build && npx jest --passWithNoTests`.

constraints: No `any` types anywhere in the model, interface, repository, or tests — use `unknown` with type guards (HARNESS.json no-any, high severity).

All database access goes through the repository layer using the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts; no inline SQL outside the repository (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository, critical).

The repository must follow the established pattern from PgEmployeeRepository/PgLeavePolicyRepository: a private inner class extending BaseRepository instantiated as `private readonly base`, a snake_case Row interface with a `[key: string]: unknown` index signature, a rowToLeaveBalance mapper, an isLeaveBalanceRow type guard using unknown (no any), and direct `this.base.query<RowType>` calls with RETURNING * rather than the generic insert/update helpers.

The entity field policyId maps to the DB column leave_policy_id (not policy_id); all other camelCase entity fields map to their snake_case DB columns (employeeId→employee_id, totalEntitlement→total_entitlement, usedDays→used_days, remainingDays→remaining_days, fiscalYear→fiscal_year, createdAt→created_at, updatedAt→updated_at).

create input is Omit<LeaveBalance,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'> with a randomUUID() id and new Date() timestamps generated inside the method; update input is Partial<Omit<LeaveBalance,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>>; upsert input is Omit<LeaveBalance,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>.

The LeaveBalance status field is an inline string union 'ACTIVE'|'EXHAUSTED'|'CLOSED' — no import from src/shared/types is required for this module (shared-types exports only LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, UserRole enums).

create throws the error message 'Failed to create leave balance' when the insert returns no row or a row failing the type guard, matching the established error-message convention from the employee and leave-policy repositories.
outOfScope: LeaveBalanceService, ILeaveBalanceService, and any business logic (deductDays, restoreDays, getAvailableBalance, initializeBalance) — these belong to Phase 9.

Enforcement of the LeaveBalance lifecycle transitions (ACTIVE→EXHAUSTED when remainingDays=0, EXHAUSTED→ACTIVE on cancellation reversal, CLOSED terminal) — the repository persists whatever status it is given; lifecycle enforcement is a service-layer concern (Phase 9).
Fastify routes, controllers, RBAC guards, and HTTP error-response mapping for leave balances — these belong to Phase 10.

Database migrations / Knex schema creation for the leave_balances table — this phase assumes the table and its unique constraint (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) already exist per the reconciled architecture.
Audit logging (GP-002) for balance create/update/upsert operations — audit wiring is a service-layer concern; the repository itself does not write audit records.

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle is ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED (when remainingDays reaches 0) or CLOSED (at fiscal-year end); EXHAUSTED → ACTIVE is permitted on cancellation reversal; CLOSED is terminal and cannot transition to any other status. The repository must not reject any of these status values but is not responsible for enforcing transition legality.

The natural key is (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear); at most one ACTIVE/EXHAUSTED balance row may exist per employee per policy per fiscal year, enforced by the unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) which upsert relies on.

remainingDays is the derived balance (totalEntitlement − usedDays); the entity is updated atomically on APPROVED and CANCELLED-from-APPROVED leave-request transitions, but the repository only persists the values it is given — it does not recompute remainingDays.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the mapped LeaveBalance or null when not found / type-guard failure; propagates underlying database errors unchanged.
Returns an array of mapped LeaveBalance rows (filtering out type-guard failures); propagates database errors unchanged.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: PgLeaveBalanceRepository must extend BaseRepository (via a private inner class) and use its generic query<T extends Record<string, unknown>> helper for all SQL, matching the BaseRepository signature in src/shared/base-repository.ts.

The repository structure (private inner BaseRepository subclass as `private readonly base`, snake_case Row interface with [key:string]:unknown index signature, rowToLeaveBalance mapper, isLeaveBalanceRow type guard using unknown, create with randomUUID id + new Date timestamps + RETURNING *, update with dynamic SET clauses + updated_at append + findById delegation, error message 'Failed to create leave balance') must mirror the established pattern in src/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.repository.ts and src/modules/employee/employee.repository.ts.

The test file must follow the established test pattern: jest.mock the db connection BEFORE importing pool, makeLeaveBalanceRow() (snake_case) and makeLeaveBalance() (camelCase) helpers, beforeEach mockQuery.mockReset(), and per-method coverage of success/not-found/type-guard-failure/error — matching tests/unit/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.repository.test.ts and tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.repository.test.ts.

The leave_balances table columns and the unique constraint (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) that upsert's ON CONFLICT targets must match the reconciled architecture's sql_schemas entry for leave_balances in .gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json.

integrationPoints.why: PgLeaveBalanceRepository extends BaseRepository and uses its query helper for all database access.
The repository (via BaseRepository) uses the exported pool for PostgreSQL queries; tests mock this module's pool.query.

Per the reconciled dependency map, leave-balance depends on leave-policy, employee, and shared-types; this phase's repository references policyId and employeeId as foreign keys to those modules' tables, though it does not import their code directly.

The ILeaveBalanceRepository interface and PgLeaveBalanceRepository created here are the data-access contract that the future LeaveBalanceService (deductDays, restoreDays, getAvailableBalance) will inject and call.
